subject: docs/coop/artifacts/route-b.DR-009.preview-disposition.v2.json
reviewType: independent, refute not confirm; one of three subjects dispatched together

advisoriesRecorded.observation: This is the only one of the three dispositions dispatched together that names an artifact without pinning it. Its appliedHeadNotThisDisposition carries a standing sentence but no path and no sha256, and its recordedInputs contains no artifact digest at all. The two siblings both pin theirs: DR-006 pins evidence-identity-recipes.v12.json at f0bfaebd… and DR-007 pins d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json at 8dd33038…, each inside the same field and again in recordedInputs. The referenced artifact exists on disk as docs/coop/artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9.json.
advisoriesRecorded.whyItIsNotABlocker: The claim the field makes is negative — 'Application of a head is not park closure and is not SATISFIED of this row' — so it does not depend on the head's exact bytes to be true, and it is independently supported by D-005, which closed application of the head rather than the parks. Nothing asserted is false and no reader is misled.
advisoriesRecorded.whyItIsWorthRaising: The artifact carries a remeasurementClause reading 'If a cited file moves, re-measure', and for this one reference there is no pinned value to re-measure against, so the clause has nothing to bite on. Both siblings show the cost is one path and one digest, and the pin would let a later reader confirm which r1 head the disposition was written against rather than resolving the name themselves.
advisoriesRecorded.suggestedFix: Add path docs/coop/artifacts/r1-lifetime-neutrality.conformance.v1.9.json with its sha256 to appliedHeadNotThisDisposition and to recordedInputs, matching the DR-006 and DR-007 form.

summary: Subject and prompt held at their dispatched digests, both read-only. Every attack axis fails and the substance is sound: applied r1 v1.9 is expressly not treated as park closure, LN-13, policyOutcome.derivationDigest and R1-PARK-* all stay open, and the artifact goes beyond file 08's needs cell by also owing CIR-B1 closure. Its DR-204 recital is true at source — I verified in an earlier cycle that the adjudication ruled the dialect-repair date anomaly 'UTC-BOUNDARY ARTIFACT, NOT A DEFECT; DR-009/R09 RELIANCE CLEAN ON THE DATE QUESTION' and recorded the D-001 gate as DISCHARGED — and this artifact correctly declines to re-open it. My single advisory is pin discipline: alone among the three dispositions dispatched together, this one names its applied head without pinning a path or digest for it.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 5e2f6572d1473176545d83ee2f8babf8daf8a3d7702ffa55bca7c7065841b782, equal to the prompt's expected value, -r--r--r-- at both ends. I verified the prompt itself against the dispatch-supplied digest 50b49de6… before relying on the subject digests it carries.

The attack 'treats applied r1 v1.9 as park closure / SATISFIED of DR-009' fails on three surfaces. appliedHeadNotThisDisposition states 'Application of a head is not park closure and is not SATISFIED of this row.' honesty states 'Preview condition 1 for this row, if later owner-recorded, closes by scoped disposition, not by park closure. D-005 closed application of the head, not the parks.' And whatThisDoesNotDo carries both 'Does not close LN-13, derivationDigest, or R1-PARK' and 'Does not treat applied r1 v1.9 as SATISFIED of those parks.'

The DR-204 recital is true at source. The artifact states 'DR-204 ruled the dialect-repair date anomaly CLEAN for reliance; this disposition does not re-open that adjudication.' I verified that adjudication directly in an earlier cycle: dr-204.re-review-independent.json records the ruling 'UTC-BOUNDARY ARTIFACT, NOT A DEFECT; DR-009/R09 RELIANCE CLEAN ON THE DATE QUESTION' and its relianceRuling records the D-001 gate — quoted there as 'DR-009 route A, gated on DR-204's adjudication of the date anomaly before reliance' — as DISCHARGED, subject to a proviso about continuing to bind the reviewed instrument digests and carry five live advisories. Declining to re-open the adjudication preserves that ruling together with its proviso rather than restating a stripped version.

rowQuoted is faithful, tested by string equality against the live row: the decision text 'R-1 identity-dependent laws and instrument standing remain conditional' and the owner 'R-1/evidence authorities' both match file 08 exactly, and statusAtAuthoring HARD-BLOCKED matches its leading label.

The d070Note claim is true in the edited register. It states 'D-070 appended a preview-scope note to other rows. DR-009 still has no scoped owner-recorded disposition.' file 08's DR-009 cell contains no 'Preview-scope owner recording' note, and D-070's condition-1 snapshot row names DR-009 among the rows that 'remain without SATISFIED or scoped owner-recorded disposition'.

whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA is a superset of file 08's needs cell rather than a reduction of it. The register asks to 'Close LN-13, policyOutcome.derivationDigest, R1-PARK-*; reviewed retained validator or explicit accepted alternative'; the artifact owes both of those and adds CIR-B1 closure. CIR-B1 is a real identifier, present in file 08, COORD and IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.

whatMustNotBePretendedSettled is correspondingly honest, listing LN-13, policyOutcome.derivationDigest, R1-PARK-*, identity-dependent R-1 implementation, 'CIR-B1 closure as a preview SATISFIED', and 'Unreviewed check-r1-v1.7.py as retained-validator standing'. That last item names a real file — check-r1-v1.7.py is present in the artifacts directory — and declines to treat it as standing, which is the conservative reading of the register's 'reviewed retained validator or explicit accepted alternative'.

The absence of a D-002 rides field is correct rather than an omission. D-002's identity-dependencies section enumerates five rides, four attaching to DR-006 and one to DR-007, and names none for DR-009 — I confirmed this by direct search in an earlier cycle, including that the apparent 'R-1' hits in D-002 are substring false positives inside 'DR-123'. The artifact instead carries the ride-shaped consequence in P-009-1's bound: identity-dependent implementation waits.

The attack 'coordinator becomes recording authority' fails: ownerWhoMustRecord names the file 08 owner and adds 'Coordinator may draft. D-000 does not make the coordinator the R-1 authority.' condition1EffectIfOwnerRecorded adds 'This file existing, or an ACCEPT verdict, is not owner recording', and whatThisDoesNotDo includes 'Does not owner-record this row.'

The attacks 'silent SATISFIED or condition-1 discharge' and 'authorizes docs/v2/implementation/' fail: status CANDIDATE-NOT-RECORDED, binds NOTHING, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, condition-1 effect scoped to 'architecture-preview scope only' with conditions 2-5 preserved and condition 5 named as the only authorization for docs/v2/implementation/, and whatThisDoesNotDo refuses both.

The selection authority is real and correctly characterised: D-072 is ADOPTED at commit 5f6b4e07bb9293041e494ab08d74942878a5af97, resolving to 'D-069/D-071/D-072: select Route B for DR-006/007/009', and whatThisDoesNotDo adds 'Does not re-adopt or overturn D-072.'

The cited digests that are present match live bytes: COORD 2af51835…, file 08 9495c70f… (the post-D-070 value), and the v1 predecessor at 2a250d88…. predecessorChange scopes the delta honestly: 'Retargets selection authority from CONTESTED D-053 to new-cycle D-072. Refreshes live pins after D-070. Does not close parks.'

P-009-1 is bounded rather than permissive: the preview may refuse reuse under the preserved one-shot/no-reuse law, but 'may not implement identity-dependent LN-13, derivationDigest, or R1-PARK items as settled.'
file 08 is unedited and git reports zero modified tracked files. I wrote three verdict files, one per subject as the prompt directs, and edited and committed nothing.

The substance of LN-13, policyOutcome.derivationDigest, R1-PARK-* and CIR-B1. I confirmed each is a real identifier in the corpus and that all are left owed; I did not audit what any of them requires.

Whether Route B is the better choice for DR-009. That was decided by D-072, which is adopted and which this artifact does not re-open.

environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256 of the prompt and all three subjects at start and again at end with ls -l for permissions; digest verification of every cited input against live bytes; git log --format=%s at full hash for the selection commit; json parse of all three dispositions to compare applied-head/live-contract pin discipline field by field, which is how the advisory was found; string-equality comparison of rowQuoted decision and owner against the live file 08 row and of statusAtAuthoring against its leading label; per-row scan for 'Preview-scope owner recording' cell notes; comparison of whatRemainsOwedOnRouteA against file 08's needs cell; corpus grep for CIR-B1 and a directory listing for check-r1-v1.7.py and the r1 v1.9 artifact; structured checks of status, binds, sealRecommendation, the coordinator-not-authority clause and the whatThisDoesNotDo refusals; git status across the tree

acceptNote: ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES at 0 blockers. The substance holds: applied r1 v1.9 is expressly not park closure, the three parks stay open, CIR-B1 is owed beyond what file 08's needs cell demands, and the unreviewed validator is refused standing rather than quietly counted. The DR-204 recital is true at source and correctly left unre-opened, which preserves that ruling's proviso rather than a stripped version of it. The advisory is not about the decision at all: this is the only one of three dispositions dispatched together that names an artifact without pinning it, which leaves its own remeasurement clause with nothing to check for that reference. Both siblings show the fix is one path and one digest.
